title: Build the local FHIR anomaly investigation demo
acceptance_criteria: Expose POST /api/v1/analyze-demo through FastAPI and make the complete local flow demonstrable from the built-in /docs interface without a separate frontend, database, upload, or arbitrary input path.

Load only the approved versioned synthetic Patient, Coverage, and ExplanationOfBenefit JSON files from dataset/, perform bounded minimal structural validation, process in memory, and prove the source files remain byte-identical.

Extract and return only the explicitly supported observed facts with stable evidence identifiers, keeping source facts, derived signals, model synthesis, missing evidence, limitations, and sanitized metadata separate.

Implement three to five transparent deterministic rules, targeting the five approved checks: reference integrity, coverage-date bounds when present, duplicate/repeated opaque product codes, a narrowly defined observed amount-component relationship, and a sample-relative high-amount signal.

Document every rule's stable ID, evaluated fields, exact formula/threshold/tolerance, evidence references, no-signal behavior, and limitations without payer-specific, terminology, fraud, coding, clinical, coverage, payment, or medical-necessity semantics.

Use the Google Gen AI SDK configured for Vertex AI for at most one no-tools model call per analysis, sending only minimized structured synthetic facts, deterministic signals, supplied evidence IDs, and limitations.

Require Pydantic-validated structured Gemini output whose candidate findings cite supplied evidence; reject unknown citations and preserve the complete deterministic report on configuration, timeout, provider, parsing, schema, or evidence-validation failure without a repair/fallback call.
Define and validate the OpenAPI contract for success, deterministic-pipeline failure, and typed Gemini success/failure states; keep the backend implementation aligned with it.

Provide focused unit and integration tests covering extraction, each rule's signal/no-signal/missing-evidence behavior, endpoint success, fake-client model success, provider failure, invalid output, unknown evidence, one-call enforcement, no live credential requirement, and dataset immutability.

Deliver a resume-quality root README with local setup, environment placeholders, architecture, rule definitions, example request/response, failure behavior, tests, limitations, and a concise resume-ready project summary; make no strict CARIN, HIPAA, production-readiness, fraud, clinical, coding, payment, coverage, or medical-necessity claim.
